report.question: Does any secret-shaped value appear in the program corpus - artifacts, event logs, transcripts, caches, test fixtures, rollback backups - and can the scanner prove it would find one if it were there?
report.answer: YES, and yes with a measured rate. (1) The command-center corpus itself is CLEAN: 715 files / 28.41 MiB including both rollback backups and the __pycache__ caches, zero gitleaks findings. (2) The EVENT LOGS are NOT clean: three distinct live Databricks personal access tokens sit in cleartext at 12 occurrences in one ledger file. Rotation is required and is the owner's action. (3) The scanner CAN prove it would find one: 20 canaries planted into a byte-mirror gave gitleaks a recall of 17/18 = 0.9444 over the well-formed baits, so the combined sweep's false-negative rate is 0.0556 (1 of 18) and the clean Tier-A verdict is reportable rather than an unmeasurable absence. (4) The single miss turned out to be worth more than the sweep itself: gitleaks' default aws-access-token rule restricts the key's trailing 16 characters to [A-Z2-7], the base32 alphabet, instead of the canonical [A-Z0-9]. Any real AWS key id containing a 0, 1, 8 or 9 anywhere in its tail is therefore silently unmatched -- measured recalls 0.1826 here and 0.1600 on a cross-vendor refuter's independent 500-candidate harness, against a closed-form 0.1519, with the base32 predicate separating fired from missed at 100% accuracy. A leaked AWS key is more likely to be MISSED than caught by a default gitleaks run. (5) Git history and the whole repo worktree are clean of the exposed token shape, bounding the incident. (6) Transcripts return 3,326 unattributed findings that are an UPPER BOUND, not a secret count, and are left NOT-CHECKED.

extensions.digest_basis: artifacts[0].sha256 is SHA-256 over this file's bytes with the 64-hex value at artifacts[0].sha256 replaced by 64 '0' characters. artifacts[0].bytes is the true on-disk byte length.
extensions.verdict_legend: REFUTED = the hypothesis 'a secret is present here' was tested and failed, i.e. the tier is clean at the measured 5.56% FN rate. CONFIRMED = a secret, or the asserted gap, was demonstrated. PARTIAL = measured but incomplete. NOT-CHECKED = not measured, with the settling experiment named in residual_unknowns.

owner_action_required.action: Rotate the three Databricks personal access tokens whose sha256[:16] fingerprints are 3ff429c671b321a1, b47b323d73b3a9cc, c8892cfe9d6e4577, covering the bolt-common, bolt-geo and datascience workspaces, and decide the remediation policy for event-ledger records that capture pasted credentials.
owner_action_required.why_not_done_here: AGENTS.md 9 reserves credential lifecycle to the owner: an agent must never remove, rotate, revoke, regenerate or otherwise modify any API key or token. The exposed ledger file was therefore left byte-untouched and is confirmed to still contain 12 occurrences.
owner_action_required.suggested_durable_fix: Fix the CONSUMER rather than the record: have the event-ledger writer redact credential-shaped substrings at write time. The estate already has a write-path redactor concept (see DC-1); the ledger path evidently does not apply it. Scoped as a RECOMMENDATION -- whether the ledger writer has a redaction hook at all was NOT measured by this unit.

canary_design.reproducibility: The artifact records the SEED and the generator recipe instead of the values, so a refuter can regenerate all 20 byte-for-byte while this file never contains a credential-shaped string (AGENTS.md 9).
canary_design.placement: Into a byte-mirror of Tiers A+B under %TEMP%, at real corpus-relative paths inside real files, across 7 surfaces (json artifact, jsonl event log, md doc, py script, txt/log, yaml-like, PEM block). NEVER into the repo -- four sibling agents were writing to it concurrently and a `git add -A` would have committed them, the one outcome the catalog forbids absolutely.
canary_design.surface_deviation: Tiers A+B contain no .toml/.yaml/.pem files, so the yaml-like and pem-block surfaces fell back to .md targets. Recorded rather than silently substituted.

vendor_shapes.malformed_reason: second JWT segment did not start with eyJ; every real JWT payload does, and gitleaks' jwt rule requires it (probe: ruleprobe variant 'header.eyJ_mid.sig' FIRED)
the 35-char part did not start with 'A'; real Telegram tokens do, and the rule requires it (probe: ruleprobe variant 'digits:A+34' FIRED)

recall_summary.why_entropy_recall_is_low: The entropy scanner's 4.0 bits/char threshold structurally cannot flag a pure-hex token: 16 symbols cap Shannon entropy at exactly log2(16) = 4.0. That is why it did NOT independently isolate the real Databricks tokens (dapi + 32 hex, measured 3.861 bits/char) -- a design flaw in PROBE 1b, disclosed rather than buried. The real exposure was found by githeaks' vendor rule and corroborated by a shape-specific regex, not by entropy.

corrections_applied.C3_line_window_artefact: entropy recall by +/-8-line window = 1.0; by exact token hash = 0.55. The window figure is WITHDRAWN as a proximity measurement.
